title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
description: A brilliant novel of manners following Elizabeth Bennet as she navigates love, reputation, and social expectations in Georgian England. Austen's witty masterpiece remains one of the most beloved works of English literature.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
description: An orphaned governess finds independence and love at the mysterious Thornfield Hall, where dark secrets lurk behind closed doors. A groundbreaking novel that blends romance, gothic atmosphere, and social commentary.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
description: Set against the terror and turmoil of the French Revolution, this sweeping novel follows the intertwined fates of two men who share a striking resemblance. Dickens delivers a powerful story of sacrifice, redemption, and resurrection.

title: Moby Dick
author: Herman Melville
description: Captain Ahab's obsessive pursuit of the great white whale drives him and his crew across the world's oceans toward a fateful confrontation. An epic meditation on obsession, fate, and the nature of evil.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
description: The wild and tempestuous love between Heathcliff and Catherine unfolds on the brooding Yorkshire moors in this passionate tale of revenge and obsession. A dark, unforgettable classic that defied the conventions of its time.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
description: Count Dracula travels from Transylvania to England in search of new blood, unleashing a trail of terror that a group of allies must unite to stop. The definitive vampire novel that defined an entire genre of horror fiction.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
description: Young orphan Pip's life is transformed by a mysterious benefactor, but his dreams of becoming a gentleman come with unexpected moral consequences. Dickens at his finest, weaving themes of wealth, loyalty, and self-discovery.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Twelve thrilling cases showcase the brilliant detective Sherlock Holmes and his faithful companion Dr. Watson as they solve baffling mysteries across Victorian London. The collection that launched the world's most famous detective.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
description: A young girl tumbles down a rabbit hole into a whimsical world filled with peculiar creatures, absurd logic, and unforgettable characters. A timeless masterpiece of nonsense literature and imagination.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
description: Victor Frankenstein's ambitious experiment to create life produces a sentient creature rejected by its maker, setting in motion a tragic chain of events. A pioneering work of science fiction and a profound meditation on responsibility and humanity.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
description: Wrongfully imprisoned, Edmond Dantès escapes, discovers a vast fortune, and meticulously orchestrates his revenge against those who betrayed him. The ultimate tale of justice, patience, and transformation.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
description: The miserly Ebenezer Scrooge is transformed after being visited by three ghosts on Christmas Eve in this beloved holiday tale. A heartwarming story of redemption that has become a cultural touchstone.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: A destitute former student commits murder and is tormented by guilt and paranoia in this gripping psychological novel set in the streets of St. Petersburg. Dostoevsky's masterful exploration of morality and the human psyche.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
description: A beautiful young man makes a Faustian bargain: his portrait ages and bears the marks of his sins while he remains eternally youthful. Wilde's only novel is a dazzling meditation on vanity, art, and moral corruption.

title: Uncle Tom's Cabin
author: Harriet Beecher Stowe
description: The harrowing experiences of enslaved people in the American South fueled the abolitionist movement and changed the course of history. A powerful novel that exposed the brutal realities of slavery to a worldwide audience.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
description: The four March sisters navigate adolescence, ambition, and love during the American Civil War in this warm and enduring family story. A timeless portrait of growing up that has charmed readers for generations.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: Young Jim Hawkins discovers a pirate's treasure map and sets sail on a thrilling voyage filled with mutiny, buried gold, and the unforgettable Long John Silver. The quintessential adventure novel that defined the genre.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
description: Martians invade Earth with devastating heat rays and towering tripods, plunging humanity into a desperate fight for survival. A pioneering science fiction epic that has terrified and inspired readers for over a century.

title: The Call of the Wild
author: Jack London
description: Buck, a domesticated dog, is stolen and sold into the brutal world of the Klondike Gold Rush, where he must rediscover his primal instincts to survive. A powerful tale of nature, resilience, and the wild within.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Sherlock Holmes investigates the legend of a spectral hound that haunts the Baskerville family on the dark and dangerous Dartmoor. The most famous of all Holmes novels, blending gothic atmosphere with brilliant deduction.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Charles Dickens
description: An orphan boy escapes the workhouse only to fall in with a gang of juvenile pickpockets led by the cunning Fagin in Victorian London. A searing indictment of social injustice wrapped in an unforgettable story of survival.

title: Robinson Crusoe
author: Daniel Defoe
description: Shipwrecked on a deserted island, Robinson Crusoe must use his wits and resourcefulness to survive alone for twenty-eight years. The archetypal castaway story that inspired centuries of adventure literature.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
description: Captain Nemo takes readers on an extraordinary submarine voyage through the world's oceans, encountering wonders and perils beneath the waves. A visionary science fiction adventure that anticipated modern submarine technology.

title: The Three Musketeers
author: Alexandre Dumas
description: Young d'Artagnan joins forces with the legendary musketeers Athos, Porthos, and Aramis in a swashbuckling tale of honor, duels, and political intrigue. A rollicking adventure that has become synonymous with daring and camaraderie.

title: Heart of Darkness
author: Joseph Conrad
description: A steamboat captain journeys deep into the Congo to find the enigmatic Mr. Kurtz, confronting the darkness at the heart of colonialism and human nature. A haunting and influential novella about civilization and its discontents.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
author: Jules Verne
description: The eccentric Phileas Fogg wagers his fortune that he can circumnavigate the globe in just eighty days, setting off on a race against time. A globe-trotting adventure filled with ingenuity, suspense, and unexpected romance.

title: Gulliver's Travels
author: Jonathan Swift
description: Lemuel Gulliver's fantastical voyages to miniature kingdoms, floating islands, and lands of rational horses satirize the follies of human society. A brilliant work of satirical fiction disguised as a travel adventure.

title: White Fang
author: Jack London
description: A wild wolf-dog navigates the harsh wilderness of the Canadian Yukon and the complexities of human civilization, learning both cruelty and compassion. A companion piece to The Call of the Wild that explores the power of love to tame the wild.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
description: Dorothy is swept by a tornado from Kansas to the magical Land of Oz, where she befriends a Scarecrow, a Tin Woodman, and a Cowardly Lion on her quest to return home. A beloved American fairy tale about friendship and courage.

title: The Jungle Book
author: Rudyard Kipling
description: Mowgli, a boy raised by wolves in the Indian jungle, learns the laws of the wild from Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther. A collection of vivid stories that explore the boundary between civilization and nature.

title: The Scarlet Letter
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: Hester Prynne bears the public shame of adultery in Puritan New England while her secret lover wrestles with guilt in this powerful moral drama. A profound exploration of sin, judgment, and the strength of the human spirit.

title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
description: Former convict Jean Valjean seeks redemption while being relentlessly pursued by the fanatical Inspector Javert against the backdrop of nineteenth-century France. Hugo's monumental epic of justice, love, and revolution.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
description: An aging nobleman, driven mad by chivalric romances, sets out as a knight-errant with his loyal squire Sancho Panza in search of adventure and glory. Widely considered the first modern novel, a satirical masterpiece about idealism and reality.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
description: An inventor travels to the distant future and discovers a divided humanity: the gentle Eloi and the terrifying Morlocks who dwell underground. A visionary work that pioneered the concept of time travel in science fiction.

title: Peter Pan
author: J. M. Barrie
description: The boy who never grows up whisks Wendy and her brothers away to Neverland for adventures with pirates, mermaids, and the vengeful Captain Hook. A magical story about the joys and bittersweet necessity of growing up.

title: The Secret Garden
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
description: A spoiled orphan girl discovers a hidden, neglected garden on her uncle's estate, and its restoration brings healing and transformation to everyone around her. A tender story of renewal, friendship, and the magic of nature.

title: The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
description: A respected London doctor invents a potion that transforms him into a depraved alter ego, unleashing the evil that lurks within every human soul. A gripping exploration of duality and the dark side of human nature.

title: Black Beauty
author: Anna Sewell
description: Told from the perspective of a magnificent horse, this novel follows Black Beauty's life from carefree colthood through hardship and kindness across Victorian England. A pioneering work of animal welfare literature that remains deeply moving.

title: The Divine Comedy
author: Dante Alighieri
description: Dante's journey through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise is an allegorical epic of the soul's path to God, populated with historical and mythological figures. One of the supreme achievements of world literature and medieval thought.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
description: The clever but misguided Emma Woodley plays matchmaker in her small village, causing humorous misunderstandings before discovering where her own heart truly lies. Austen's most technically accomplished comedy of manners.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
description: The Dashwood sisters, practical Elinor and passionate Marianne, navigate love, loss, and financial hardship in Regency England. Austen's debut novel contrasts two approaches to life and love with her signature wit.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
description: Anne Elliot, persuaded years ago to break her engagement, meets Captain Wentworth again and must confront lingering feelings and second chances. Austen's most mature and emotionally nuanced novel about constancy and regret.

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
description: Mole, Rat, Toad, and Badger share charming adventures along the riverbank and in the Wild Wood in this beloved children's classic. A gentle, humorous tale of friendship, nature, and the simple pleasures of life.

title: Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
description: Gregor Samsa awakens one morning to find himself transformed into a monstrous insect, forcing his family to confront their dependence on him and their own grotesque transformations. A surreal and unsettling masterpiece of modernist literature.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
description: A scientist discovers how to make himself invisible but becomes increasingly unstable and dangerous as his power isolates him from society. A thrilling science fiction novel about the corrupting influence of unchecked ambition.

title: The Lost World
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
description: Professor Challenger leads an expedition to a remote South American plateau where prehistoric creatures still roam, challenging everything known about natural history. A thrilling adventure that inspired countless dinosaur stories and films.

title: From the Earth to the Moon
author: Jules Verne
description: Members of a post-Civil War gun club devise an audacious plan to launch a projectile to the Moon using a colossal cannon. A remarkably prescient science fiction novel that anticipated many aspects of space travel.

title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
author: Jules Verne
description: Professor Lidenbrock and his nephew descend into an Icelandic volcano and discover a vast subterranean world filled with prehistoric wonders and perils. A classic scientific romance that captures the thrill of exploration and discovery.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
description: Machiavelli's notorious treatise on political power offers pragmatic, often ruthless advice to rulers on how to acquire and maintain control. A foundational work of political philosophy that continues to provoke debate centuries later.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
description: An ancient Chinese military treatise that presents strategies for warfare and conflict that have been applied to business, politics, and life for over two millennia. A timeless guide to strategy, leadership, and tactical thinking.

title: The Murders in the Rue Morgue
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: C. Auguste Dupin, the first fictional detective, uses brilliant analytical reasoning to solve a gruesome double murder in Paris that baffles the police. The story that established the detective fiction genre.

title: The Fall of the House of Usher
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: A visitor is drawn into the claustrophobic world of his troubled friend Roderick Usher and the decaying mansion that seems to share the family's cursed fate. A masterclass in gothic atmosphere and psychological horror.

title: The Tell-Tale Heart
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: A murderer's guilt manifests as a phantom heartbeat that grows ever louder, driving him to madness and confession. Poe's quintessential tale of psychological terror and the inescapable weight of conscience.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
description: Odysseus battles monsters, witches, and the wrath of the gods on his epic ten-year voyage home from the Trojan War. One of the foundational works of Western literature, a timeless adventure of heroism and perseverance.

title: The Iliad
author: Homer
description: The wrath of Achilles drives the action of this epic poem set during the Trojan War, exploring themes of honor, fate, and the cost of war. The oldest and greatest epic of Greek literature.

title: Through the Looking-Glass
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Alice steps through a mirror into a world of reversed logic, where she meets Tweedledum and Tweedledee, the Red Queen, and the Jabberwock. A dazzling sequel that rivals its predecessor in whimsy and imagination.

title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
author: Mark Twain
description: Tom Sawyer's mischievous adventures along the Mississippi River include witnessing a murder, getting lost in a cave, and whitewashing a fence. A joyous celebration of American boyhood and the spirit of adventure.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
description: Huck Finn and the runaway slave Jim float down the Mississippi on a raft, encountering a vivid cross-section of American society. Often called the Great American Novel, a profound commentary on freedom and racism.

title: David Copperfield
author: Charles Dickens
description: From a difficult childhood to his eventual success as a writer, David Copperfield's journey mirrors Dickens's own life in this richly autobiographical novel. A sprawling, emotionally resonant tale of perseverance and growth.

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L. M. Montgomery
description: An imaginative, talkative orphan girl transforms the lives of her adoptive family on Prince Edward Island with her irrepressible spirit. A beloved coming-of-age story filled with warmth, humor, and heart.

title: The Phantom of the Opera
author: Gaston Leroux
description: A masked musical genius haunts the Paris Opéra House, obsessed with a young soprano in this atmospheric tale of love, obsession, and dark secrets. The gothic thriller behind one of the world's most famous stage musicals.

title: The Thirty-Nine Steps
author: John Buchan
description: An innocent man becomes entangled in a deadly espionage plot and must flee across Scotland while unraveling a conspiracy that threatens national security. The prototype of the modern thriller novel.

title: The Turn of the Screw
author: Henry James
description: A young governess at a remote country estate becomes convinced that the orphaned children in her care are being corrupted by malevolent ghosts. An ambiguously terrifying novella that has spawned countless interpretations.

title: King Solomon's Mines
author: H. Rider Haggard
description: Allan Quatermain leads an expedition into uncharted African territory in search of a lost diamond mine and a missing brother. A landmark adventure novel that established many tropes of the lost-world genre.

title: The House of the Seven Gables
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
description: The cursed Pyncheon family is haunted by the sins of their ancestors in a decaying New England mansion with seven gables. A brooding gothic romance that explores the weight of the past on the present.

title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
author: Washington Irving
description: The superstitious schoolteacher Ichabod Crane encounters the legendary Headless Horseman in the eerie village of Sleepy Hollow. A classic American ghost story blending folklore, humor, and suspense.

title: The Moonstone
author: Wilkie Collins
description: A stolen Indian diamond with a cursed history passes through many hands, each owner beset by misfortune, until the mystery of its theft is finally solved. Widely considered the first full-length detective novel in English.

title: The Prisoner of Zenda
author: Anthony Hope
description: An Englishman visiting the fictional European kingdom of Ruritania is forced to impersonate the kidnapped king in this dashing tale of honor and romance. The classic Ruritanian romance that spawned an entire subgenre.

title: The Woman in White
author: Wilkie Collins
description: A mysterious woman in white appears on a moonlit road and sets in motion a complex plot of identity, fraud, and madness in Victorian England. A gripping sensation novel that kept Victorian readers on the edge of their seats.

title: The Mystery of Edwin Drood
author: Charles Dickens
description: Dickens's final, unfinished novel centers on the disappearance of young Edwin Drood and the suspicion that falls on his uncle, the opium-addled choirmaster John Jasper. A tantalizing literary mystery that remains unsolved.

title: The Island of Doctor Moreau
author: H. G. Wells
description: A shipwrecked man finds himself on an island where a mad scientist creates grotesque hybrid creatures through vivisection. A disturbing meditation on evolution, cruelty, and what it means to be human.

title: Northanger Abbey
author: Jane Austen
description: Young Catherine Morland's imagination runs wild with gothic novels as she visits the mysterious Northanger Abbey, leading to humorous misunderstandings. Austen's playful parody of sensational fiction and a delightful coming-of-age story.

title: The Last of the Mohicans
author: James Fenimore Cooper
description: During the French and Indian War, the frontiersman Natty Bumppo guides two daughters of a British officer through the dangerous wilderness of colonial America. A thrilling historical adventure of courage and survival.

title: The Autobiography of Benjamin Franklin
author: Benjamin Franklin
description: One of America's founding fathers recounts his remarkable life, from humble beginnings to scientific achievement and political prominence. An inspiring account of self-improvement, ingenuity, and the American spirit.

title: A Modest Proposal
author: Jonathan Swift
description: Swift's devastating satirical essay suggests that the Irish should sell their children as food to wealthy English landlords to alleviate poverty. A masterwork of dark political satire that retains its bite centuries later.

title: Mansfield Park
author: Jane Austen
description: The quiet and principled Fanny Price must navigate the complexities of wealth, status, and morality at her wealthy relatives' estate. Austen's most morally serious novel, exploring themes of constancy and integrity.

title: She
author: H. Rider Haggard
description: Two explorers discover a mysterious African kingdom ruled by Ayesha, an immortal queen who has waited two thousand years for her lost love. A thrilling blend of romance, adventure, and the supernatural.

title: Uncle Remus: His Songs and His Sayings
author: Joel Chandler Harris
description: The tales of Br'er Rabbit and other animal characters are woven together by the wise and gentle Uncle Remus in this collection of African American folk tales. A foundational work of American folklore storytelling.

title: The Narrative of Arthur Gordon Pym of Nantucket
author: Edgar Allan Poe
description: A young stowaway embarks on a harrowing sea voyage to the South Pole, encountering mutiny, shipwreck, and unexplainable horrors along the way. Poe's only complete novel is a gripping tale of maritime terror.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Five aristocratic families navigate love, loss, and the Napoleonic Wars in this monumental Russian epic that interweaves personal drama with grand historical events. Widely regarded as one of the greatest novels ever written.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
description: The Prince of Denmark is visited by his father's ghost and charged with avenging his murder, setting in motion a tragic chain of events. Shakespeare's most celebrated play explores mortality, madness, and the burden of conscience.

title: Walden
author: Henry David Thoreau
description: Thoreau's account of two years living simply in a cabin near Walden Pond is a profound meditation on nature, self-reliance, and the examined life. A foundational text of American transcendentalism and environmental thought.
